evals.prompt: From a CI shell I need the last 30 daily bars for AAPL via the Twelve Data CLI, as JSON I can pipe to jq. Show the exact commands including how to auth without interactive login.
evals.expected_output: Exports TWELVEDATA_API_KEY (the name the binary reads) and runs twelvedata time-series with --symbol AAPL --interval 1day --outputsize 30; no interactive login and no --api-key on the command line.
assertions: Uses the twelvedata CLI binary (not raw curl to api.twelvedata.com as the primary path)
Authenticates through the TWELVEDATA_API_KEY environment variable rather than passing --api-key on the command line
Runs time-series with interval 1day and outputsize 30 (or equivalent flags)
Does not rely on interactive twelvedata login as the only auth method for CI
Says the first bar is the newest unless an ascending order is requested

evals.prompt: Get the 14-day RSI for AAPL with the Twelve Data CLI. I tried `twelvedata rsi` and it failed.
evals.expected_output: Uses twelvedata ti rsi with --symbol AAPL --interval 1day --time-period 14 and explains indicators live under ti.
assertions: Uses twelvedata ti rsi (or ti <indicator>), not a top-level rsi command
Passes time-period 14 and an interval such as 1day
Explains that indicators are under the ti subcommand

evals.prompt: Our agent subprocess calls the Twelve Data CLI and sometimes gets a non-zero exit. How should we discover valid flags, and where do errors go so stdout stays pipeable?
evals.expected_output: Points at twelvedata commands for discovery, errors on stderr as JSON, stdout response-only, and stable exit codes such as 3 for auth.
assertions: Recommends twelvedata commands (or schema) instead of scraping --help as the source of truth
States that errors go to stderr (JSON envelope) while stdout stays the response
Mentions at least one stable exit code category such as auth=3 or rate limit=6
